clue.text: Prudence requires new directions

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of the next word are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Being careful means following a fresh set of instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an adjective for the directions, but it signals that the ten letters of DIRECTIONS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name good judgement and caution in what one says or does.

clue.text: Daring yet quite mild oath

explanation.surface: Someone bold who swears only gently.
explanation.definitionFit: Verve or flair is one sense; the other is the genteel expletive used instead of a stronger curse, as in 'Oh, bother!'.

clue.text: Super sort of doctor — he's the tops!

indicators.note: sort of tells us the word Super is to be sorted into another order

parts.note: MO is the Medical Officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: Praise for a brilliant physician who is the best of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Super' seems to praise the doctor, but 'sort of' means its letters are sorted, giving SUPRE; MO is the usual army abbreviation for Medical Officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the overall boss, the person at the very top of an organisation.

clue.text: Blimpish types race into strange heavenly constellation

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of race and into are made odd, mixed up into a new order

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is a constellation of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Fogeyish people hurtling towards an odd star sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges two clue words together, making REACTION. Colonel Blimp was a British cartoon character, a pompous diehard opposed to change.
explanation.definitionFit: Blimpish people are stuffy conservatives who resist progress, the very picture of political diehards.

clue.text: Worries with money time's overcoming?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece overcoming another sits above it, so the time letter goes on top

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
roubles are the money of Russia

explanation.surface: Anxieties about cash being outrun by the passage of time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'overcoming' places T above ROUBLES, the Russian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are nouns for cares and anxieties that weigh on someone.

clue.text: Creature with unusual brio, one finds

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of brio appear in an uncommon order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An animal with remarkable vigour is what one discovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges BRIO into ORIB; I (one) is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Boom that can be reversed by strikes?

indicators.note: can be reversed tells us the word for strikes is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks or blows

explanation.surface: A loud noise that hitting something might turn around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boom' looks like a loud noise but is the nautical spar; RAPS (strikes) is turned round by 'can be reversed'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing boat the boom is a horizontal pole holding the sail's foot, a kind of mast-like pole.

clue.text: Round of newspapers to own

indicators.note: Round says the word for newspapers goes around the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively
taken as written

explanation.surface: A paper round, delivering the newspapers you possess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a paper boy's delivery route, but it is a container signal: the newspapers go around the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: To own is to admit or declare openly, as when one claims or avows a belief.

clue.text: Inappropriate spectacles for the pessimist

parts.note: glasses that make everything look rosy would suit an optimist, so a gloomy person would never wear them

explanation.surface: The wrong eyewear for someone who always expects the worst.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing through rosy glasses means viewing things too hopefully, the opposite of a gloomy outlook.

clue.text: Wild ape is brown

indicators.note: Wild tells us the letters of ape and is run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An untamed primate turns out to be brown-coloured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' looks like a description of the ape, but it signals that APE and IS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colour, named after the cuttlefish ink once used as a pigment.

clue.text: Defaults and assignments come to nothing

indicators.note: come to means the assignments arrive at and attach to the nothing piece, following it

parts.note: O is the zero digit, nothing
missions are tasks or assignments given to someone

explanation.surface: Failures to pay, and tasks that end up worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come to' joins MISSIONS onto the end of O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: A default is a failure to do something required, which is a neglect or oversight.

clue.text: Driven wild in the classrooms?

parts.note: the surface suggests pupils maddening a teacher, but it reads as the teachers who are in charge of the classrooms, driven to distraction there

explanation.surface: Someone pushed to distraction by unruly pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers in charge of classrooms are the ones most likely to be exasperated by pupils.

clue.text: The mine blasts shaking the powers that be

indicators.note: shaking tells us the letters of the preceding three words are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: Explosions underground rattle those in authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' rearranges all the letters of THE MINE BLASTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruling group that holds authority in society is called by both names.

clue.text: Discreet testimony initially taken into consideration

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate testifying to a qualification

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Tactful evidence being weighed up at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks as if it belongs to 'testimony' alone, but it covers the three words that follow it; a diploma testifies to a qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tactful and careful in dealings with others is what a diplomat does, hence both words.

clue.text: Mince pies, too, with sulphur, providing atomic elements

indicators.note: Mince tells us the words that follow are chopped up and their letters rearranged

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A recipe of chopped pies with brimstone, offered as chemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince' looks like the Christmas pie filling but signals a rearrangement, making ISOTOPE; the chemical symbol for sulphur completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopes are forms of a chemical element differing in the number of neutrons in their atoms.

clue.text: Firm employing most that is relative

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: most means all but the final letter of the word for employing is taken

parts.note: using means employing

explanation.surface: A company that uses most of its staff is family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' leaves off the last letter of the synonym for employing, giving USIN; 'that is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, the child of an aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Officials dealing with death of duck in traps

indicators.note: in tells us the duck goes inside the word for traps

parts.note: to corner someone is to trap them, so corners means traps
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: People investigating a bird killed by a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is a cricket score of nought, O, put 'in' CORNERS (traps).
explanation.definitionFit: Coroners hold inquests into sudden or unexplained deaths.

clue.text: Gear for cattlemen hitting a trail

indicators.note: hitting suggests the letters of a and trail are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Cowboys' kit as they set off along the trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitting a trail' sounds like setting off, but 'hitting' scrambles A TRAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a rope with a running noose used by cowboys to catch livestock, a lasso.

clue.text: Concern about letting arrangement being free!

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a lease is a contract by which property is let

explanation.surface: Worries about a rental agreement give way to liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is only a link to the definition; 'Concern about' misleads as worry, but it reads as the short word for concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: To release is to let go or liberate someone.

clue.text: In favour of withdrawing alum from key prescriptions

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in 'all those for'

indicators.note: withdrawing means the word alum is drawn back, read in reverse

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Supporting removal of the astringent from the chemist's key ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' turns ALUM into MULA; E is a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula is a recipe or set of instructions for making something, as a prescription is.

clue.text: Finally departed, though is stuck in first gear

indicators.note: is stuck in says the word for though is wedged inside the word for departed

parts.note: late means dead, someone who has finally departed this life
yet means though, nevertheless

explanation.surface: Somebody at last leaves, though stuck in bottom gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first gear' looks like motoring but means a baby's first clothes; YET 'is stuck in' LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the set of clothing and bedding for a newborn baby, its first outfit.

clue.text: New film you'll use includes first lyric — flowing sweetly as honey

indicators.note: includes says the shuffled letters take in the next piece
New tells us the letters of the following words are put into a fresh order
first means only the opening letter of lyric is used

explanation.surface: A fresh film score using a first song that flows like honey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges FILM YOU'LL USE, and that 'includes' L, the 'first' of lyric.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellifluous comes from Latin words for honey and flow, describing smooth sweet sound.

clue.text: See and take advantage of the bloodsucker

parts.note: lo means look or see, as in 'lo and behold'
to use someone is to exploit them

explanation.surface: Watch out for the parasite and exploit it.
explanation.walkthrough: LO (see) is followed by USE (take advantage of).
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a parasitic insect that feeds on its host's blood.

clue.text: English trifle upset, arriving at this unusual island

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for trifle reads upwards

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, something of little value

explanation.surface: A tipped-over English pudding arrives at an odd islet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' looks like the pudding, but means TOY, which 'upset' turns over after E. 'arriving at this unusual' is padding to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small island in a river, such as those in the Thames.

clue.text: Start off with menu change

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of Start and menu are thrown off course into a new order

explanation.surface: Kicking off a meal with a menu alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' looks like beginning, but 'off' scrambles START and MENU.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmute is to transform something into another form or substance.

clue.text: No way out for the book-keeper!

definitions.text: No way out for the book-keeper!

parts.words: No way out for the book-keeper!
parts.note: the surface suggests an accountant trapped, but a way in, not out, is meant, and also what an accountant records in a ledger

explanation.surface: An accountant finds themself trapped with no escape.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a way in, the opposite of an exit, and an item recorded in an account book.

clue.text: Cook ide's head, taken from the main

indicators.note: taken from says the letter that follows is removed from the word for main

parts.note: main and chief both mean principal

indicators.note: head means the first letter of ide's is used

explanation.surface: Someone prepares a fish whose head has been taken from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The ide is a freshwater fish and 'the main' looks like the sea; 'head' gives I, 'taken from' CHIEF (main) to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook in a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Dogged badger nips setter

indicators.note: badger means harass, and the harassed letters of nips and setter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A determined badger bites a gun dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' looks like the animal biting a setter, but it is a verb that scrambles NIPS SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone who keeps going stubbornly and refuses to give up.
